To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) contextual explanation networks learn to predict and generate explanations jointly, (ii) the generated explanations are valid instance-specific approximations of the decision boundary of the network, (iii) the generated explanations act as a regularizer and boost performance in low-resource setting.

(i) contextual explanation networks are a novel deep learning approach that jointly predicts and explains; (ii) contextual explanation networks generate valid explanations that can be used to interpret predictions; and (iii) contextual explanation networks improve predictive performance and are competitive with the current state-of-the-art.
(i) CENs learn contextual explanations and (ii) they boost the performance of the model in low-resource settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions: (1) Can we learn to explain? and (2) How can we learn to explain and predict jointly?
the problem of model explanation.
the question of whether we can build a single model that is both a predictor and an explanation tool, with the latter being learned from data, rather than being post-hoc engineered.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CEN approach offers a novel, interesting and competitive approach to explain and predict simultaneously, and that it can be applied in a variety of different settings.
our model offers the best of both worlds: it learns to predict and explain, and its predictions are supported by valid explanations.
our model can be used to generate explanations for any deep network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel class of models that can be seen as a combination of deep networks and probabilistic graphical models.
we propose a novel class of models that can generate valid explanations for each of their predictions, while also being competitive with state-of-the-art models in performance.
we propose a new class of models that can learn to predict and explain jointly.

the explanation generation process can be used as a powerful regularization mechanism, boosting predictive performance in low-data regimes.
